It took the Morean name in 2009 after donor Beth Morean funded the Central Avenue buildings, then in 2010 brought the Chihuly Collection to town, which drew 250,000 visitors in its first five months and now sits across the street at 720 Central.
morean-arts-center.descriptor: Community art center at 719 Central Ave, home to the Chihuly Collection

mr-empanada.text: A family-run Tampa Bay chain started by Audrey Perez with Al Perez and Lisa Ferras, which held its grand opening in 2003 and now lists nine locations around the bay. The draw is the empanada case — beef and cheese, pizza, guava and cream cheese — alongside Cuban sandwiches, black bean soup and cafe con leche.
mr-empanada.descriptor: Latin counter for empanadas and Cuban sandwiches, part of a Tampa Bay chain

mr-mrs-crab.text: By the company's own telling, its founders came home from a spring 2016 trip to New Orleans hooked on Louisiana seafood boils and recreated them in Florida with an Asian twist: the house special seasoning blends Cajun, lemon pepper, garlic butter and Szechuan spices, and everything arrives in a boil bag with no fork or knife required.
mr-mrs-crab.descriptor: Cajun-Asian seafood-boil chain outpost on US 19 in Pinellas Park

mr-sushi.descriptor: Sushi, hibachi and bento restaurant at 1310 34th St N

museum-of-fine-arts.text: St. Petersburg's first art museum, opened in 1965 on a four-acre waterfront site the city donated, thanks to collector Margaret Acheson Stuart, who seeded it with a $1 million endowment and works from her own collection. Its original wing was designed by architect John Volk; the collection now spans some 20,000 objects across nearly 5,000 years.
museum-of-fine-arts.descriptor: Encyclopedic art museum on the Beach Drive waterfront since 1965

my-rich-uncle.text: It opened at 260 1st Ave N in the space left behind by 260 First, the downtown nightclub that had closed the year before, from Forward Hospitality Group — the group behind Goodnight John Boy. The draw is martinis and a retro lounge, an "Uncle's Stash" list that runs to Van Winkle bourbon and Louis XIII cognac, and a Millionaire Monday on the first Monday of the month where the door hands you $10 instead of charging cover.
my-rich-uncle.descriptor: Martini bar and retro lounge on 1st Ave N, open Fridays and Saturdays

natures-table.text: This is an outpost of Nature's Table, a health-food cafe franchise that bills itself as a legacy brand dating to 1977. The menu is the chain's: sandwiches, wraps, salads, protein bowls, smoothies and acai bowls, mostly feeding the downtown weekday lunch crowd — it closes by 7 p.m. and doesn't open weekends.
natures-table.descriptor: Nature's Table cafe off Sunshine Lane N — wraps, salads, smoothies

neighborhood-joe.text: A mostly vegan neighborhood café known for its vegan BLT (marinated tempeh, avocado, arugula and sprouts) and hard-to-resist blueberry muffins. It closed its original spot just up the block on MLK at the end of December and reopened six weeks later on February 15, 2024, in the plaza next to Trip's Diner, with more patio space.
neighborhood-joe.descriptor: Mostly vegan café and coffee shop on MLK Jr St N next to Trip's Diner

nine-spices-hot-pot.text: Cook-at-the-table hot pot and Korean BBQ where trays of ingredients ride out to you on a conveyor belt, and the kitchen stays open until 1 a.m. every night. A sister Nine Spices now operates in Clearwater on Countryside Blvd.
nine-spices-hot-pot.descriptor: Conveyor-belt hot pot and Korean BBQ on 66th St N in Pinellas Park

nitallys.text: A husband-and-wife Thai-Mexican fusion spot best known for the Inferno Soup Challenge: a 48-ounce, $50 bowl loaded with peppers including ghost chilies. Food Network's Heat Seekers filmed chefs Aaron Sanchez and Roger Mooking attempting it when no one had ever finished; a Gainesville writer eventually conquered it. Nitally's later moved from Central Avenue to 9th Street North.
nitallys.descriptor: Thai-Mex mom-and-pop on 9th St N, home of the Inferno Soup Challenge

nori-thai.text: A Thai-and-Japanese spot on Blind Pass Road known for its pad thai and sushi; the restaurant says it has been voted 'Best of the Beaches' for both Thai food and sushi eight years running.
nori-thai.descriptor: Thai and sushi restaurant on Blind Pass Road in St. Pete Beach

north-shore-kickball-fields.text: The ball diamond at 33-acre North Shore Park, steps north of downtown on Tampa Bay, is St. Pete's kickball home: Tampa Bay Club Sport stages its Monday "Big Ball" coed league here, 10-on-10 with a 10-inch ball, with post-game drink specials at a sponsor bar.
north-shore-kickball-fields.descriptor: Softball diamond at waterfront North Shore Park used for coed kickball leagues

north-shore-volleyball-courts.text: Six sand courts on the downtown waterfront at North Shore Park, free on a first-come basis (or rentable), sharing the complex with the North Shore Aquatic Complex pool, tennis courts and a lighted softball field.
north-shore-volleyball-courts.descriptor: Six free beach volleyball courts on the bay at North Shore Park, 901 North Shore Dr NE

north-straub-park.text: Named for William Straub, the St. Petersburg Times editor who crusaded to turn the bayfront into public parkland — the city secured the waterfront lots in 1908–09, a deal the Times called "the best Christmas present St. Petersburg ever had." In the 1920s developer C. Perry Snell shipped some thirty classical statues from Italy for the waterfront parks; only a weathered handful still stand here.
north-straub-park.descriptor: Downtown bayfront lawn with a concert stage on Bayshore Dr NE

nueva-cantina.text: Opened in 2016 by Raul Medina with a kitchen staffed largely by cooks from Mexico City and Jalisco, Nueva Cantina built its reputation on Mexican street food (the birria is the signature) and fresh-squeezed margaritas. The restaurant is now 100% employee-owned and announced a second location in downtown Tampa for 2025.
nueva-cantina.descriptor: Mexican street-food and margarita spot at 1625 4th St S in south St. Pete, since 2016

oak-and-stone.text: Opened July 9, 2018 as the second location of a Sarasota concept, next to the Hyatt Place at the foot of Central. Its claim to fame is the region's largest self-serve beer wall: an RFID wristband unlocks roughly 50 rotating craft taps, bills by the ounce and cuts you off at 40 ounces. Wood-fired pizzas and a 3,000-square-foot deck round it out.
oak-and-stone.descriptor: Wood-fired pizza and self-pour craft beer wall at 199 Central Ave

off-the-brick-new-york-pizza.text: This family-owned pizzeria at 49th St N and 73rd Ave has been baking here since 1999, originally under the name Central Pizza before rebranding as Off The Brick. The dough is still hand-tossed and slid into brick-lined deck ovens on wooden peels, and they run their own delivery drivers instead of third-party apps.
off-the-brick-new-york-pizza.descriptor: NY-style brick-oven pizzeria on 49th St N, since 1999 (ex-Central Pizza)

writtenFor.name: Off The Brick New York Pizza

old-northeast-tavern.text: The Old Northeast's "Cheers" bar sits in a 1925 building that was a WWII servicemen's bar, the N&L Diner, a laundromat and a yoga studio before the tavern opened in 2006. Bob Wareham and Mark Brindle have run it since 2008; it closed in late 2024 to build a shared dining room connecting it to next-door Old Northeast Pizza, and it plans to reopen with a newly acquired liquor license and cocktails for the first time.
old-northeast-tavern.descriptor: Neighborhood pub on 7th Ave N in the Old Northeast, open since 2006

old-southeast-market.descriptor: Corner poke bar, deli and beer market at 3rd St S and 17th Ave in Old Southeast

one-night-stand.descriptor: Small smoking bar at 149 1st Ave N in downtown St. Petersburg

overflow-brewing-company.text: Sour-beer specialist opened in spring 2018 in a converted office building behind the Morean Arts Center by Troy Bledsoe, a homebrewer-turned-Rapp Brewing brewer, with friends Ryan Sarno and Jessica Holder. Its tap handles were built from Bledsoe's own childhood Legos, some 30 years old. After eight years, it poured its last beers in August 2026.
overflow-brewing-company.descriptor: Sour-focused microbrewery on 1st Ave N with Lego-built tap handles (2018–2026)

oyster-shucker-craft-draft.descriptor: Family-owned waterfront oyster bar with 50+ beers at 650 Corey Ave, St. Pete Beach

pacific-counter.text: This 660 Central storefront is where Pacific Counter started in 2018: three industry veterans (Tanner Loebel, sushi chef Tock Noythanongsay, and Eric Bialik) launched a build-your-own poke bowl and sushi burrito counter that has since grown into a Tampa Bay chain and spent years running a stand at Tropicana Field. Regulars know it for the pineapple soft serve and Spam musubi.
pacific-counter.descriptor: Fast-casual poke bowl and sushi burrito counter on Central Ave, since 2018

paisanos-pizza-pasta.text: A 4th Street North fixture since 1974, still family-owned and billing itself as St. Pete's Italian-American classic — the dough, sauces, soups and dressings are prepped daily from family recipes, and a salad bar and full liquor bar sit alongside the pizza and pasta.
paisanos-pizza-pasta.descriptor: Family-owned Italian-American pizza and pasta spot on 4th St N since 1974

pana-kava-java.text: A neighborhood kava bar more than a coffeehouse: the house pour is kava made fresh daily, served alongside kratom brews, nitrogen-infused teas and locally roasted coffee. It's one of five Pana locations around Tampa Bay, and the greeting on the wall is the South Pacific toast that comes with the shell — "Shells up, Bula!"
pana-kava-java.descriptor: Kava bar and coffee shop on 66th Street North in Pinellas Park

paolos-pizza-subs.text: Actually spelled Paulo's, this pizza-and-sub shop has been run by Joe and Maria Santos since 1983. Regulars swear by the sauce and the calzones.
paolos-pizza-subs.descriptor: Family-run pizza and sub shop in St. Petersburg, since 1983

paradeco-coffee-roasters.text: Owners Tom and Sonya built the name out of "paradise" — their word for St. Pete — and the art deco look they love. It's independent rather than a franchise, roasts its own beans in-house on a zero-emission Bellwether roaster, and has a second, poolside bar at SkyBeach Resort.
paradeco-coffee-roasters.descriptor: In-house coffee roaster at 111 2nd Ave NE, off Beach Drive

paradise-grille-pass-a-grille.text: This beachfront site held the La Plaza Hotel and then the Pass-a-Grille Hotel, both lost to fire (1922 and 1967), before record producer Phil Gernhard, of 'Snoopy vs. the Red Baron' fame, convinced the city in 1970 to let him build a concession stand so kids would stop crossing the road for sodas. It is still the only concession directly on Pass-a-Grille Beach, and each evening someone rings the old ship's bell at sunset.
paradise-grille-pass-a-grille.descriptor: City-owned beach bar and grill on the sand at Gulf Way, Pass-a-Grille

paradise-grille-upham-beach.text: The sister location of the Pass-a-Grille original, this beach concession sits right on the sand at Upham Beach in St. Pete Beach. Locals still remember the stand by its old name, the Seaside Grille, before it was rebranded; it opens at 7am and closes a half hour past sunset daily.
paradise-grille-upham-beach.descriptor: Beach concession on the sand at Upham Beach, open 7am to past sunset

park-rec.text: Stephen Schrutt's Hunger + Thirst group turned downtown's old World of Beer into a game bar in early 2017: Skee-Ball, air hockey, vintage cabinets from Galaga to Mortal Kombat and a turfed cornhole patio, anchoring a First Avenue S block shared with sister spots The Avenue and Proper. The neon over the bar reads 'youth has no age.'
park-rec.descriptor: Arcade-and-lawn-games bar on 1st Ave S downtown, opened 2017

parkshore-grill.text: Open since 1996, Parkshore Grill bills itself as the first major restaurant on Beach Drive, setting the template for the sidewalk-dining strip that followed. Partner and executive chef Tyson Grant runs the modern American menu, served al fresco with waterfront views.
parkshore-grill.descriptor: Modern American sidewalk-dining restaurant on Beach Drive NE since 1996

parkside-cafe.text: A 7 a.m.-to-2 p.m. neighborhood diner — omelets, breakfast skillets, Cuban sandwiches and a bakery case — that also runs a full liquor bar, so mimosas and bloody marys are on the breakfast menu. Closed Tuesdays.
parkside-cafe.descriptor: Breakfast-and-lunch diner at 8180 49th St N, Pinellas Park

pasadena-yacht-country-club.text: Opened in 1924 as the golf club for Jack Taylor's boom-era Pasadena-on-the-Gulf development, with golf legend Walter Hagen as co-owner and first club pro. It was Bear Creek, then Boca Ciega, before settling on this name; U.S. Steel reconfigured the course and added the marina in the 1980s, and the club says Babe Ruth, Arnold Palmer and Michael Jordan have all teed it up here.
pasadena-yacht-country-club.descriptor: Private golf and yacht club in Gulfport, founded 1924

pee-pas-garage-craft-brewery.text: Jim Brown spent nearly 40 years running North St. Pete Collision, then built a brewing setup for himself in Georgia and decided "why should I have all the fun?" — so the old collision shop became Pee-Pa's Garage. It pours house beers, distills small-batch moonshine and bourbon, grills burgers at the Wood Shed Grill, and throws axes in the Hatchet Barn.
pee-pas-garage-craft-brewery.descriptor: Craft brewery and distillery in a former collision shop, 6340 49th St N

perrys-bbq.text: Founder Perry opened the first Perry's BBQ in 1998 out of a passion for traditional Chinese-style BBQ, and the chain has grown to six Tampa Bay locations; the draw is a pick-your-meats plate — BBQ, orange, honey, Mongolian, black pepper or blackened chicken and pork — served over rice.
perrys-bbq.descriptor: Asian-style BBQ chicken-and-pork rice-plate counter inside Tyrone Square Mall

perrys-porch.text: Named for C. Perry Snell, the 1920s developer who shaped much of downtown, it opened on the St. Pete Pier in February 2025 in the former Hops & Props space. Owner Ryan Griffin calls it his 'love letter to St. Pete,' down to cocktails named for the Pink Streets and Jungle Prada.
perrys-porch.descriptor: Coastal eatery with a waterfront porch at the St. Pete Pier, opened 2025

pho-ha-tien.descriptor: Vietnamese pho house on Park Blvd in Pinellas Park

pho-kien-giang.text: A Pinellas Park pho institution that stays packed without social media, marketing or even an updated website. In August 2025 it moved a few blocks down 49th Street into the former Nam Viet building, and regulars lined up for the first service. Known for beef-bone pho, ultra-crispy chicken wings and bún bowls, with a second location planned at 5800 34th St N.
pho-kien-giang.descriptor: No-frills Vietnamese pho house on 49th St N in Pinellas Park

pho-quyen-vietnamese.text: Pho Quyen has been ladling pho in Pinellas Park since 1998, and its own kitchen claims the best noodle soup in the Tampa Bay area. The cooking leans on fresh herbs and vegetables with a light hand on the oil, aiming at both healthy eating and full flavor.
pho-quyen-vietnamese.descriptor: Vietnamese pho house in Pinellas Park, open since 1998

pier-teaki.text: The open-air tiki bar on the roof of the Pier head, five floors up at the end of the St. Pete Pier — about as far into Tampa Bay as you can get without getting wet. It sits in the $92 million, 26-acre Pier District that opened July 6, 2020, and is run by the same local owners as Birchwood and The Canopy on Beach Drive.
pier-teaki.descriptor: Rooftop tiki bar on the 5th floor of the St. Pete Pier head

pin-on-grand.text: Opened in the Grand Central District in November 2024 when owners Som and Roger Rattanachane relocated their Pin On Cafe from the EDGE District and refocused it on Thai and northern Laotian cooking — Som is from Thailand, Roger from Laos, and the family previously ran Pin Wok & Bowl and Sab Cafe. Expect Lao-style papaya salad with wild rice noodles alongside sushi stacks, sushi burritos and a full liquor bar.
pin-on-grand.descriptor: Thai and Lao fast-casual with sushi and a full bar, 2458 Central Ave

pin-wok-bowl.text: A Thai-and-Japanese fusion spot on the 400 block of Central, known for sushi burritos and poke bowls alongside pad thai and green curry. Owners Som and Roger Rattanachane went on to open a second concept, Pin On Café, in the Edge District in 2021, staffed almost entirely by relatives and friends.
pin-wok-bowl.descriptor: Thai-Japanese fusion spot on the 400 block of Central Ave (sushi burritos, poke)

pineapple-espresso.text: Founded by Tara and Laurene, this Dr. MLK Jr Street drive-thru pairs coffee with actual breakfast — avocado toast with eggs on sourdough, a pea and charred carrot frittata, wellness teas. They skipped the speaker box on purpose: orders are taken face to face at the window, because they wanted to know every guest by name.
pineapple-espresso.descriptor: Drive-thru coffee and healthy breakfast on Dr. MLK Jr St N

pioneer-park.text: This small waterfront park between Central Ave and 1st Ave S honors St. Pete's founders: a 20-foot obelisk at its center carries bronze plaques naming about 600 early settlers who lived in the area before January 1, 1912. Jay B. Starkey Sr. launched the memorial drive in 1976 and the park was dedicated on November 26, 1981; a descendant-run foundation still funds its upkeep after a 2012 revitalization.
pioneer-park.descriptor: 1.8-acre pioneer memorial park on Bayshore Dr near Al Lang Field

pipos.text: The Hernandez family opened the first Pipo's Cuban cafe in Tampa in 1979 and still cooks from the same family recipes at this Bay Pines outpost. Pipo's is a three-time winner of the Ybor Cuban Sandwich Competition and chef-owner Ramon Hernandez a two-time Top Local Chef champ; the roast pork is the house calling card.
pipos.descriptor: Family-run Cuban cafe on Bay Pines Blvd; Tampa roots since 1979

pipos-cuban-cafe.descriptor: Counter-service Cuban cafe on 4th Street N in north St. Pete

poke-island.text: A counter-service poke shop at 7093 66th Street North where bowls get assembled in front of you off a topping line; the sushi burrito is the other signature order, and there's bubble tea alongside. Regulars mostly talk about the portion size — one bowl routinely stretches into two meals.
poke-island.descriptor: Build-your-own poke bowls and sushi burritos on 66th St N, Pinellas Park

poppos-taquiera.text: A family-run taqueria named after the owner's grandfather, "Poppo," that models its burritos and tacos on the Mission District street food of San Francisco — homemade flour and corn tortillas, fresh and organic ingredients, and 12-inch flour-tortilla burritos, served from a storefront at 1033 Central Ave.
poppos-taquiera.descriptor: Cali-style Mexican street food counter at 1033 Central Ave with homemade tortillas

porters-stone-soup-cafe.text: Now trading as Stone Soup Cafe & Pub, it is a made-to-order sandwich and homemade-soup counter with a full bar and around 50 beers, and a regular fixture on local hidden-gem roundups.
porters-stone-soup-cafe.descriptor: Soup-and-sandwich cafe with a 50-beer pub on 16th Street N

quan-ngon-bistro.descriptor: Vietnamese buffet on Park Blvd in Pinellas Park — pho, bánh xèo, bò kho

rec-dec.text: Rec Dec is a bar built around a sandlot: sand volleyball courts outside, an indoor rec room for darts and cornhole, and year-round leagues run through Tampa Bay Club Sport. It sits at 380 105th Terrace NE, with the bar opening at 5:30 p.m. on weekdays and 11 a.m. on weekends.
rec-dec.descriptor: Sand volleyball bar in St. Pete with year-round leagues and a rec room

red-white-booze.text: For years this waterfront spot on Pass-a-Grille Way was Sea Critters Cafe, a fixture for boaters and beach vacationers; new owners took it over and rebranded it Red, White & Booze in 2022, keeping the docks, local grouper and margaritas and adding live music on the deck.
red-white-booze.descriptor: Dockside seafood bar on the Intracoastal in Pass-a-Grille, pull up by boat

renzos.text: The downtown flagship of a Tampa-born Argentine steakhouse that started on Kennedy Boulevard in 2009: steaks fired over quebracho wood in a Josper oven, house-made empanadas and a wine list poured from Mendoza outward, a couple of blocks from the Pier.
renzos.descriptor: Argentine steakhouse and wine bar at 2nd St S and 1st Ave S, since 2018

rewind-st-pete.text: Opened on 1 August 2026 in the room that had been the sports bar Who's On First, whose co-owner Mike Jennings is among the four owners here. The theme is 1990s and 2000s nostalgia: murals of characters from the era's cartoons, films, games and adverts, roller-rink carpet, period music, and a Blockbuster-themed menu.
rewind-st-pete.descriptor: '90s and 2000s themed bar at 119 1st Ave N, open since August 2026

ricks-reef.text: Something has been serving food on this corner since 1939, when Larry's Luncheonette opened as a drive-up hot dog stand; the owners say the original floor is still underfoot. After runs as Capt. Zak's, Spoonbills, Bobby's Place and The Reef, a regular bought the place and reopened it as Rick's Reef in August 2012, keeping the old name.
ricks-reef.descriptor: Casual seafood-and-burger bar on Gulf Blvd at 68th Ave, St. Pete Beach

right-around-the-corner.text: Opened in fall 2016 by two local beer enthusiasts, John McMahan and Tom Rockhill (founder of the St. Pete Brew Club), it bills itself as St. Pete's first craft-beer-and-retro-arcade bar. In April 2018 they converted a former gelato kitchen in the 1,400-square-foot space into a working brewery, which the Catalyst reported was believed to be Florida's only full 'arcade brewery.'
right-around-the-corner.descriptor: Retro arcade bar and nano-brewery on Central Ave in the Grand Central District

riptides.text: A no-kitchen beach dive at 7618 Blind Pass Road that runs 1 p.m. to 3 a.m. seven days a week — snacks only, plus a jukebox, a pool table and dart boards. The late-night crowd is beach regulars, off-duty service workers and people not ready to call it a night.
riptides.descriptor: Late-night dive bar on Blind Pass Road in St. Pete Beach

rococo-steak.text: Opened in October 2013 inside the historic 1920s former YWCA building on 2nd Avenue South. Named for the ornate Rococo art period, it set out to break the idea that a steakhouse is only for special occasions, pairing a modern steak menu with a wine list that has run to more than 600 labels.
rococo-steak.descriptor: Upscale modern steakhouse in the 1920s former YWCA building on 2nd Ave S, opened 2013

root-clay.text: Root + Clay is the restaurant at 170 47th Avenue NE — the address of the member-owned Racquet Club of St. Petersburg — so a night out here comes with tennis courts next door. The kitchen makes things from scratch, including soups, and runs to braised short ribs, chimichurri chicken and salads, with a full bar and a shaded patio.
root-clay.descriptor: Scratch-kitchen restaurant and bar at the Racquet Club on 47th Ave NE

roses.descriptor: Coffee shop at 1234 Central Ave, downtown St. Petersburg

round-lake.text: The surrounding Round Lake Historic District — about a thousand historic buildings roughly bounded by 5th and 13th Avenues N — was added to the National Register of Historic Places on September 29, 2003. The neighborhood has since merged with S. Crescent and Uptown to become Historic Uptown.
round-lake.descriptor: Small lake in St. Pete's Historic Uptown neighborhood

rubys-elixir.text: Ruby's grew out of Central Cigars, a cigar shop that opened on Central Avenue in the late 1990s; in 2011 the owners bolted on Ruby's Elixir as a live-music lounge. It now books musicians every night of the week, and the Thursday jazz sessions in its leather-clad "Havana Room" are the local draw.
rubys-elixir.descriptor: Cigar-and-jazz lounge off Central Ave with live music seven nights a week

rum-runners.descriptor: Bar with outdoor seating in St. Pete Beach

rumfish-grill-bar.text: The sports-bar half of RumFish Grill at the TradeWinds' RumFish Beach Resort, where the 700-gallon Predator Tank is full of lionfish — the invasive Pacific species the display urges diners to order off the menu to help control. Big-screen TVs, a deck, and the RFG Fish Tank, a 40-ounce cocktail served in a keepsake fishbowl, round it out.
rumfish-grill-bar.descriptor: Sports bar and deck at RumFish Beach Resort with a 700-gallon lionfish tank

rumfish-grill-restaurant.text: You eat beside a 33,500-gallon saltwater aquarium that fills an entire wall — built by Wayde King and Brett Raymer of Acrylic Tank Manufacturing after Guy Harvey and the resort's president challenged them on an hour-long episode of Animal Planet's Tanked. The tank holds Gulf natives like snook, grouper, tarpon and a green moray eel, and the resort even runs a snorkel program that lets guests swim in it.
rumfish-grill-restaurant.descriptor: Seafood restaurant at RumFish Beach Resort with a 33,500-gallon aquarium

sab-cafe.text: Founded in 2011 by Melanie Rattanachane, whose family came from Laos; the name Sab means "yummy" in Laotian. It opened in the Plaza Tower courtyard as a Southeast Asian fast-casual spot built around bánh mì, and has since grown into a Thai-Vietnamese-Japanese cafe with a sake cocktail bar.
sab-cafe.descriptor: Thai-Vietnamese-Japanese cafe and sake bar in the Plaza Tower courtyard downtown

saigon-blonde.text: In 2018 St. Pete local Peri Bandazian turned the former LUX lounge at 265 Central into a semi-fictional slice of 1960s Saigon: five rooms of tiki totems and murals by local artist Jean Michael Fait, including a tiny "military bar" built from an old airplane wing and a VIP loft under a muraled ceiling.
saigon-blonde.descriptor: '60s-Saigon tiki cocktail bar at 265 Central Ave, opened 2018

saint-pete-bagel-company.text: Around since 1987, this is the St. Petersburg shop of a small four-store Pinellas chain that hand-rolls New York-style bagels and makes its own donuts, cream cheese and coffee roasts in house; Creative Loafing readers have kept it among Tampa Bay's favorite bagel shops for more than a decade.
saint-pete-bagel-company.descriptor: NY-style bagel and donut bakery on 4th St N, around since 1987

saint-pete-brewing-company.text: Opened in 2014, two years after St. Pete legalized microbreweries. When founder Tom Williams first planned a brewery there were none in the city; by the time his opened it was number five. Flagships St. Pete Orange Wheat and Milo's IPA are canned across Florida's west coast, and in 2021 it took over the storefront next door for an event space called The Nest.
saint-pete-brewing-company.descriptor: Downtown craft brewery on 1st Ave N, home of St. Pete Orange Wheat

saint-petersburg-ale-house.text: This is the St. Pete outpost of Miller's Ale House, the sports-bar chain Jack Miller started in Jupiter, Florida in 1988. Its locations were traditionally named for their town (the older ones were simply "Gainesville Ale House" and so on), which is why it shows up on the map as "Saint Petersburg Ale House". Inside: 60-plus TVs, 35 taps, and the chain's hand-breaded Zingers.
saint-petersburg-ale-house.descriptor: Miller's Ale House sports bar on MLK Jr St N near Gateway Mall

salems-fresh-eats.text: Salem's started in Tampa in 1988, when founder Salem decided fast food ought to match a sit-down restaurant for quality — nothing gets cooked until you order, from gyros and wings to salads and seafood. It has since grown to 14 Tampa Bay locations, including this one on 34th Street N.
salems-fresh-eats.descriptor: Cooked-to-order gyros and wings on 34th St N; Tampa Bay chain since 1988

saltys-tiki-bar-beach-lounge.text: It's a beach bar at the TradeWinds Island Grand, a 28-acre, 381-room resort at 5500 Gulf Blvd — the one with the waterway you can ride a paddleboat down and a three-story waterslide.
saltys-tiki-bar-beach-lounge.descriptor: Beach bar at the TradeWinds Island Grand resort, St. Pete Beach

sams-sushi.text: Sam had run just one restaurant before, a small Chinese place in Minnesota, and was nearly 15 years out of the business when he and his wife opened this spot in late 2019 next to the movie theater in the Shoppes at Park Place. Locals come for Chef Nini's rolls, including a Tiger Roll with mango salsa and an oversized lobster roll served half in a martini glass.
sams-sushi.descriptor: Sushi restaurant next to the movie theater at Shoppes at Park Place, since 2019

sawatdee-thai-and-sushi.descriptor: Thai kitchen and sushi bar on Park Boulevard in Pinellas Park

sawgrass-lake-park.text: This 400-acre park started life in 1972 as a flood-control project to protect Pinellas Park, and its water-control structure still doubles as natural water treatment for runoff headed to Tampa Bay. The boardwalk runs through one of the largest maple swamps on the Gulf Coast, with an observation tower over the lake, resident alligators, and thousands of migrating birds passing through each spring and fall.
sawgrass-lake-park.descriptor: 400-acre county park with a boardwalk through a maple swamp and a tower

sculleys.text: Sculley's sits on the boardwalk of John's Pass, the historic fishing village in Madeira Beach. The restaurant went dark under its previous owner during the pandemic, was bought along with The Hut Bar & Grill and six boat slips in a $5 million deal by Treasure Island developer Bill Karns, then renovated and relaunched with a Gulf-to-table menu and its loaded Bloody Marys.
sculleys.descriptor: Waterfront seafood restaurant on the John's Pass boardwalk in Madeira Beach

seasons-cafe-bakery.text: It opened in 2011 as a small coffee shop and grew into a full-service cafe. The kitchen now runs Vietnamese, Thai, Lao and Korean side by side, with the Vietnamese sandwiches as the calling card.
seasons-cafe-bakery.descriptor: Vietnamese-Thai-Lao cafe and bakery on US 19 in Pinellas Park

senor-taco.text: Señor Taco Cantina serves homemade tacos, burritos and fajitas out of rooms 1, 2 and 3 of an old Park Boulevard motel — I Love the Burg calls the food "revelatory" and the building "a kitschy old motel."
senor-taco.descriptor: Family-owned Mexican cantina in a converted motel on Park Blvd, Pinellas Park

shadracks.text: A red-neon dive in Pass-a-Grille pouring cheap beer since 1972, famously described as a wooden shack turned inside out, with a shingled roof built on the inside. Fishermen, bikers and beach regulars pack it on the first Sunday of every month for the legendary Bloody Mary bar, where you buy the vodka and load a skewer with bacon, meatballs, wings and cheese from the garnish buffet.
shadracks.descriptor: Cash-only dive bar on 8th Ave in Pass-a-Grille since 1972; first-Sunday Bloody Mary bar

shells.text: Shells started in Tampa in 1985 when Swiss chef John Christen bet on fresh seafood at dockside prices over fancy decor; the chain grew to 28 restaurants, and its clam chowder has drawn notice from Gourmet Magazine since 1988. The St. Pete Beach location was revived in 2016 by the founder's son under a 20-foot thatched tiki roof, near where a Shells had first stood around 1990.
shells.descriptor: Casual seafood house with a thatched tiki roof on Gulf Blvd, St. Pete Beach

shrimpys-waterfront.text: Open since 2012 and run by a family that moved down from Atlanta, Shrimpys pairs Florida seafood with New Orleans cooking — shrimp and grits, po'boys, jambalaya, a shrimp boil — with indoor and outdoor seating on the Intracoastal and live music on the schedule. It traded for years as Shrimpy's Blues Bistro before rebranding to Shrimpys Waterfront.
shrimpys-waterfront.descriptor: Waterfront seafood with a New Orleans accent on Blind Pass Rd since 2012

siam-garden.text: St. Pete's longest-running Thai restaurant, opened in 1988 by chef Piboon "Boone", who learned to cook in Bangkok and bills it as the city's first Thai restaurant back when the cuisine was still a novelty in Tampa Bay. Its signature offer is "Bring Your Catch": hand over the fish you landed (cleaned and fileted) and the kitchen turns it into a multi-course meal with appetizer, soup, entrée and jasmine rice.
siam-garden.descriptor: Thai restaurant on Dr. MLK Jr. St N in Allendale Park, est. 1988

sila-thai.descriptor: Neighborhood Thai restaurant on 49th St N at 38th Ave N

skyway-jacks.text: Founded in 1976 by Jack Thomas as a small shack at O'Neill's Marina feeding commercial boaters and fishermen, the all-day-breakfast joint later moved up to 34th Street South. Look for the giant Humpty Dumpty and rooster out front, and order the scrapple, which the Food Network once crowned Florida's best breakfast dish.
skyway-jacks.descriptor: All-day country breakfast diner on 34th St S since 1976

slice-of-the-burg.text: A locally owned slice shop out on Roosevelt Boulevard near Gateway Crossings, doing New York-style pies with housemade sauce and fresh dough alongside wings, cheesesteaks and strombolis. It also claims one of the largest vegan pizza menus in the area — the house motto is "keeping St. Pete weird, fed, and extra cheesy."
slice-of-the-burg.descriptor: New York-style pizza and cheesesteaks on Roosevelt Blvd in Gateway

snappers-sea-grill.text: Fisherman-turned-restaurateur Dan Casey opened Snappers on Valentine's Day 1998 after a dozen years running Dan's Beachside Deli, a business he'd started as a hot dog stand on July 4, 1986 with $86 in first-day sales. Fresh grouper from local fishermen was the deli's calling card, and Casey himself won the King of the Beach fishing tournament in 2017; his son Connor now helps run the place.
snappers-sea-grill.descriptor: Gulf seafood and dry-aged steaks on Gulf Blvd, St. Pete Beach, since 1998

snell-arcade.text: Developer C. Perry Snell filled this 1928 Mediterranean Revival building with tiles and artwork he collected on European trips, running an arcade of imported Italian, Spanish, and Cuban tile from Central Avenue through to the Open Air Post Office. He mortgaged it to fund Snell Isle and lost it in 1933 during the Depression; a planned second tower was never built. The arcade was walled off in 1950, reopened in a 1980s renovation that uncovered an Italian mosaic of Venice's Santa Maria della Salute, and the building became condos in the 2000s.
snell-arcade.descriptor: 1928 Mediterranean Revival landmark at 405 Central Ave, on the National Register

south-straub-park.text: Named for William Straub, the St. Petersburg Times editor who crusaded for years to keep the downtown shoreline as public parkland rather than commercial waterfront. The city announced the land acquisition on Christmas Eve 1909, which his paper called "the best Christmas present that St. Petersburg ever had." The south half now sits beside the Museum of Fine Arts and hosts festivals and art fairs.
south-straub-park.descriptor: Downtown waterfront park lawn beside the Museum of Fine Arts

southside-craft-coffee-brew-bar.text: A favorite stop of the organizer of St. Pete's Craft Coffee Tour, who named it among the city's best specialty-coffee shops alongside Bandit and Craft Kafe.
southside-craft-coffee-brew-bar.descriptor: Dog-friendly indie coffee shop with vegan pastries on 6th St S

spa-beach-bistro.text: The St. Pete Pier's only open-air cafe, sitting at Spa Beach beside the Majeed Foundation splash pad and the first trolley stop — pizza and cold drinks for people coming straight off the sand. The 26-acre Pier District it anchors opened on July 6, 2020.
spa-beach-bistro.descriptor: Outdoor pizza-and-drinks cafe at Spa Beach on the St. Pete Pier

special-pho.descriptor: Vietnamese hole-in-the-wall pho spot at 1390 34th St N

spring-garden.text: A neighborhood takeout counter at 850 49th Street North working the full American-Chinese canon — General Tso's, sesame chicken, egg foo young, lo mein, and a "Happy Family" that piles crab meat, pork, shrimp, beef and chicken into one plate.
spring-garden.descriptor: American-Chinese takeout counter on 49th Street North

spring-garden-family-restaurant.descriptor: Old-school breakfast-and-lunch diner on 62nd Ave N, open 7am–3pm daily

st-pete-pier.text: St. Pete has had a pier on this spot since 1905's Electric Pier, followed by the 1926 Million Dollar Pier and the inverted-pyramid pier of 1973, which was demolished in 2015. The current 26-acre, $92M Pier District opened in July 2020 with restaurants, Tampa Bay Watch's Discovery Center and Janet Echelman's floating net sculpture Bending Arc.
st-pete-pier.descriptor: 26-acre downtown waterfront pier district on Tampa Bay, opened 2020

st-petersburg-museum-of-history.text: Founded in 1920, this is the oldest museum in Pinellas County; the city gave it the site after the 1921 hurricane wiped out the aquarium that stood there. Its centerpiece is a full-size replica of the Benoist airboat that made the world's first scheduled commercial airline flight, St. Petersburg to Tampa, on January 1, 1914, and it also holds Little Cooperstown, the largest collection of signed baseballs in the world.
st-petersburg-museum-of-history.descriptor: City history museum on 2nd Ave NE, home to the 1914 first-airline Benoist replica

stillwaters-tavern.text: Opened in June 2015 in the old Bruce Watters Jewelers space on Beach Drive by the group behind BellaBrava a few doors down. The opening menu was built by Top Chef season 10 alum Jeffrey Jew, and the kitchen still sells itself as a from-scratch American tavern leaning on local fish, farms and regional craft beer.
stillwaters-tavern.descriptor: American scratch kitchen and bar on Beach Drive since 2015

sumitra-espresso-lounge.text: Opened in 2019 in the restored 1926 Business Center on Gulfport's Beach Blvd, this coffee lounge was started by cannabinoid scientist Maurice Loeb, who claims it was the first brick-and-mortar business in Florida to offer CBD. In 2021 Loeb bought the whole five-business building to keep a real estate company from snapping it up, calling it the biggest sale in downtown Gulfport.
sumitra-espresso-lounge.descriptor: Coffee lounge in the 1926 Business Center at 2838 Beach Blvd S, Gulfport, since 2019

sunken-gardens.text: A century-old botanical garden that began as a sinkhole: plumber George Turner Sr. bought the lot in 1903, drained its shallow lake, and found the rich muck grew just about anything. He started charging a nickel for tours in the 1930s, and the city bought the gardens in 1999 to save them from redevelopment — today it's four acres of tropical plants, flamingos, and one of St. Pete's oldest roadside attractions.

sunset-grille.text: A longtime neighborhood bar and grill at 2996 MLK Jr St N: a small horseshoe bar and pool tables up front, and out back a beer-garden patio with a brick-laid bar, arched windows and a stage for live music. Regulars swear by the fried mushrooms and wings.
sunset-grille.descriptor: Neighborhood bar & grill with pool tables and a big back patio on MLK St N

sushi-inc.text: A downtown Japanese restaurant and bar on 1st Ave N that has served hand-rolled sushi alongside regular live music since it opened in late 2013.
sushi-inc.descriptor: Downtown sushi bar with live music on 1st Ave N, since late 2013

sushi-rock-grill.descriptor: Sushi bar in the Sun Blvd plaza on Isla del Sol

sushi-sho-rexley.text: Brought omakase to downtown St. Pete in January 2018, when brothers Arte and Rexley Kwok, who previously ran Lazy Maguro in Palm Harbor, opened it near 2nd Street North. Chef Rexley, trained under master sushi chef Hiro Ida and making sushi in the area since 1999, serves a chef's-choice progression of up to a dozen courses in an 800-square-foot room; it holds a MICHELIN Recommended listing, retained in the 2026 guide.
sushi-sho-rexley.descriptor: Omakase sushi counter on 2nd St N, open since 2018

swigwam-beach-bar.text: Swigwam started as an open-air beach-bar shack on St. Pete Beach; when the attached hotel changed hands, the bar's manager kept the name and reopened it on Corey Avenue, where it's now a dollar-bills-on-the-wall locals' dive billed as home of the famous Bushwacker and Rum Runner.
swigwam-beach-bar.descriptor: Locals' dive bar on Corey Ave, St. Pete Beach, known for frozen Bushwackers

tampa-bay-watch-discovery-center.text: The nonprofit Tampa Bay Watch's marine education center at the St. Pete Pier, opened alongside the new Pier in 2020. Touch tanks, a wet lab, and exhibits on the bay's oysters, seagrass, and sea life make it the science stop on a Pier walk.

tasty-pho.descriptor: Vietnamese restaurant on 49th St N in Pinellas Park

ted-peters-smoked-fish.text: Ted Peters found a discarded smoker just after World War II and put it out front by the road so people could see and smell it; the family has been smoking mullet, mackerel, mahi and salmon over red oak in the same brown wooden building on Pasadena Ave since around 1950. Still cash-only, still open-air picnic tables, still run by the founder's descendants, with the German potato salad recipe from 'Mom' Tilla Lathrop.
ted-peters-smoked-fish.descriptor: Open-air smoked-fish shack on Pasadena Ave since 1950, cash only

tequila-daisy.text: Opened July 1, 2023 by Monique Grespan and Melissa Powell (also a partner in nearby Pour Judgement), who planned a 100-150 bottle collection and ended up with more than 500 tequilas and agave spirits, one of the largest tequila bars in the U.S. The name nods to the margarita's origin story: "margarita" means "daisy," and legend says the drink was born when a bartender grabbed tequila instead of brandy for a Brandy Daisy.
tequila-daisy.descriptor: Bright tequila-and-mezcal cocktail bar on 1st Ave N, opened 2023

terra-mar-brazilian-steakhouse.text: A family-run Brazilian churrascaria started in 1999 by Geraldo and Marlete Ferreira, who brought the rodizio format with them from Brazil: carvers work the room with skewers off an open fire until you flip your card. The house's headline cut is picanha, the salt-crusted sirloin cap, backed by a salad bar and whole pineapples glazed in brown sugar and cinnamon.
terra-mar-brazilian-steakhouse.descriptor: Brazilian churrascaria on 49th St N in Pinellas Park since 1999

thai-am.text: One of St. Pete's oldest Thai restaurants, a 4th Street North fixture for more than 20 years, run by a Thai-born owner and head chef cooking with ingredients imported from Thailand. The showpiece is Chicken on Fire (gai fai), a fried chicken breast in spicy chili sauce that arrives flaming with whiskey; the cheese-stuffed tempura chicken wings are the other local favorite.
thai-am.descriptor: Family-run Thai restaurant at 6040 4th St N, a fixture for 20+ years

the-ale-and-the-witch.text: This taphouse opened in early 2011 under Brett Andress with a single rule: every tap pours American craft beer, 32 of them at launch. Tucked in the Tower Plaza courtyard between Beach Drive and BayWalk, it has hosted live local music in its courtyard for over a decade and is beloved as one of downtown's craft-beer third places.
the-ale-and-the-witch.descriptor: American craft beer taphouse in the Tower Plaza courtyard off Beach Drive

the-bends.text: Opened in 2012 and billing itself as a "classy dive bar," The Bends is St. Pete's go-to spot for cheap drinks and free live shows, with local and touring bands and monthly DJ residencies packing a back room that I Love the Burg called "a secret portal to the underground."
the-bends.descriptor: "Classy dive bar" with free live music at 919 1st Ave N, since 2012

the-bikery.text: Taylor Norton opened this coffee-shop-inside-a-bike-shop with his father Neal in 2016 after seeing the bikes-and-coffee cafes of Colorado; it sits a block off the Pinellas Trail in Grand Central, pours Buddy Brew coffee, and was one of only four Florida dealers for hand-made Moots titanium bikes.
the-bikery.descriptor: Coffee bar + bike shop on 1st Ave S near the Pinellas Trail, since 2016

the-burg-bar-grill.text: Owner Bill Georgiou grew up in his family's Greek restaurants after they moved from Windsor, Ontario to Florida in the early 1980s and opened Grecian Gardens on Seminole Blvd, and his mother Maria's recipes still shape the menu here. That heritage is why a burger bar's signature item is a gyro feta burger.
the-burg-bar-grill.descriptor: Family-run burger pub on Central Ave, known for its gyro feta burger

the-burg-diner.text: The sister spot to The Burg Bar & Grill on Central Ave, opened by owner Bill Georgiou as what he calls 'a throwback to the diners that I grew up in' — classic breakfast-lunch diner fare with a Greek and Cuban accent, from gyro and Cuban breakfast sandwiches to pressed Cubans.
the-burg-diner.descriptor: Classic diner on 49th St N, sister to The Burg Bar & Grill

the-cabana-bar.text: The toes-in-the-sand bar at RumFish Beach Resort, with live music, frozen drinks and bar bites. Every evening staff strike a gong for the "Sunset Shot" as the sun drops into the Gulf — a TradeWinds tradition — and the resort's RumFish Grill next door houses a 33,500-gallon aquarium.
the-cabana-bar.descriptor: Beachside resort bar at TradeWinds' RumFish Beach Resort, St. Pete Beach

the-campus-grind.descriptor: Coffee shop and breakfast cafe in St. Petersburg

the-canopy.text: The rooftop lounge on top of The Birchwood, a 1924 building that started life as the Lantern Lane Apartments, the only apartments on Beach Drive facing the bay, and later ran as Grayl's Hotel. Developer Chuck Prather bought it at a foreclosure auction, restored it, added two floors and reopened it in 2013 as a boutique hotel, with the Canopy up top giving one of downtown's best views over the waterfront and Tampa Bay.
the-canopy.descriptor: Rooftop cocktail lounge atop the Birchwood hotel on Beach Drive

the-canopy-at-birchwood.text: The rooftop lounge on top of The Birchwood, a 1924 building that started life as the Lantern Lane Apartments, the only apartments on Beach Drive facing the bay, and later ran as Grayl's Hotel. Developer Chuck Prather bought it at a foreclosure auction, restored it, added two floors and reopened it in 2013 as a boutique hotel, with the Canopy up top giving one of downtown's best views over the waterfront and Tampa Bay.
the-canopy-at-birchwood.descriptor: Rooftop cocktail lounge atop the Birchwood hotel on Beach Drive

the-chattaway.text: Built in the early 1920s as a general store, it became a sandwich-and-beer joint after Prohibition ended and is one of St. Pete's longest-lived restaurants; nobody, not even longtime owner Helen Lund, ever figured out what the name means. Lund bought it in 1951 and her family ran it for 75 years. Jillian Frers, the London-born 'Lady Chattaway' who married into the family, added the English tea room in 1999 and had the facade painted pink; 44 painted bathtubs planted with flowers ring the patio. In 2026 a group including Ferg's owner Mark Ferguson bought it to keep it open.
the-chattaway.descriptor: Pink patio sandwich-and-beer joint with an English tea room, 4th St & 22nd Ave S

the-crafty-squirrel.text: Opened in late 2018 in the old Fortunato's Italian Kitchen space on the 200 block of Central, with two industrial garage doors that roll up to the street. Owner Cameron, who grew up in the Australian outback, was so taken with squirrels on arriving in the US that he named the pub after them; inside, an exposed brick wall carries a century-old Palace Ice Cream Parlor mural.
the-crafty-squirrel.descriptor: High-energy pub and dance bar with garage doors on Central Ave, since 2018

the-dali-museum.text: Home to the largest collection of Salvador Dalí's work outside Europe, built from the private collection of Ohio industrialist A. Reynolds Morse and his wife Eleanor, who chose St. Petersburg for it in 1982. The 2011 waterfront building's free-form glass bubble, nicknamed the Enigma, nods to the geodesic dome on Dalí's own museum in Figueres, Spain.

the-don-cesar.text: The 'Pink Palace' opened in 1928, built by developer Thomas Rowe as a tribute to a lost love, and drew Jazz Age names like F. Scott Fitzgerald and Al Capone. The Army bought it in 1942 as a military hospital, the government left in 1969, and a citizens' 'Save the Don' campaign rescued it from demolition before a 1973 reopening. Hurricanes Helene and Milton forced a long closure in 2024; it reopened in March 2025.
the-don-cesar.descriptor: Pink 1928 Mediterranean-style beach resort hotel on St. Pete Beach

the-drunken-clam.text: Just across from the beach access, this orange-and-teal beach dive is known for its "naked" wings — the Cajun-Parmesan-garlic recipe took first place at the 2009 Wingstock contest among local beach bars. Look for the mural of a beer-drinking clam on the building across the street.
the-drunken-clam.descriptor: Beach dive bar off Gulf Blvd in St. Pete Beach known for naked wings

the-floribbean.text: A counter-service Caribbean-fusion bowl shop in the Grand Central District, blending flavors from Africa, India, Asia, Latin America and Florida — think the signature 'Yardbird' bowl or Cuban-style pork with ginger black beans, sweet plantains and coconut rice, washed down with tropical spiked juices.
the-floribbean.descriptor: Counter-service Caribbean-fusion bowls on Central Ave in Grand Central

the-floridian-cuban-sandwiches.text: Open since 1993 on the Treasure Island Causeway, this family-run counter was named Best Cuban Sandwich in Tampa Bay by the St. Petersburg Times and FOX 13's favorite Cuban. Its version stacks ham, spiced pork, Genoa salami and Swiss on Cuban bread, eaten on an open-air deck.
the-floridian-cuban-sandwiches.descriptor: Cuban sandwich shop on the Treasure Island Causeway since 1993

the-galley.text: Opened in late 2016 by St. Pete natives Pete Boland and Ian Taylor, who met on the St. Pete High wrestling team, in the old Reno's Downtown Joint space across from the historic open-air post office. It bills itself as a late-night steak and seafood spot, serving a full menu until 2 a.m., and every January it throws a pre-Gasparilla "Shipwrecked" party where the whole bar shows up in pirate gear.
the-galley.descriptor: Late-night tavern with steak, seafood and Cuban sandwiches at 27 4th St N

the-galley-a-st-pete-tavern.text: Opened in late 2016 by St. Pete natives Pete Boland and Ian Taylor, who met on the St. Pete High wrestling team, in the old Reno's Downtown Joint space across from the historic open-air post office. It bills itself as a late-night steak and seafood spot, serving a full menu until 2 a.m., and every January it throws a pre-Gasparilla "Shipwrecked" party where the whole bar shows up in pirate gear.
the-galley-a-st-pete-tavern.descriptor: Late-night tavern with steak, seafood and Cuban sandwiches at 27 4th St N

writtenFor.name: The Galley - A St. Pete Tavern

the-garage-on-central.text: A no-frills gay dive in the Grand Central District, loosely automotive-themed: diecast cars over the beer cooler, a wall of old license plates, and a U-shaped bar top embedded with spark plugs and tools. Karaoke nights, DJs, a country-music Thursday, cheap drinks and a big patio have made it a Pride-weekend fixture.
the-garage-on-central.descriptor: Automotive-themed gay dive bar in the Grand Central District, 2700 block

the-island-grille-raw-bar.descriptor: Seafood grill and raw bar with weekend breakfast on Madonna Blvd in Tierra Verde

the-james-museum.text: Opened in April 2018 by businessman Tom James and his wife Mary, who spent about $75 million turning their private collection of Western and wildlife art into a downtown museum. The building uses veined sandstone to mimic the canyons of the American Southwest, with carvings meant to evoke the Mesa Verde cliff dwellings.
the-james-museum.descriptor: Western and wildlife art museum in downtown St. Pete, opened 2018

the-lemon-grass.descriptor: Thai and sushi tapas restaurant at 310 Central Ave downtown

writtenFor.name: The Lemon Grass - Central Arts District

the-library.text: Opened in 2018 as The Peabody, the St. Pete sister of Tampa's Oxford Exchange, and renamed The Library about five months later in homage to its namesake, Baltimore's George Peabody Library. It feeds the Johns Hopkins All Children's campus from morning coffee through dinner, with an all-day coffee bar and cocktails.
the-library.descriptor: Oxford Exchange's café-restaurant inside Johns Hopkins All Children's, since 2018

the-oyster-bar.text: A downtown fixture on Central Avenue from 1999, taken over in 2013 by Australian restaurateur Josh Cameron and known for its oyster platters, lobster rolls and buffalo shrimp. It closed in August 2023 for what was meant to be a six-month move; the 2024 hurricane season and contractor delays stretched that to two years, and it reopened October 14, 2025 in a larger 3,200-square-foot space 20 blocks west at 2245 Central in the Grand Central District.
the-oyster-bar.descriptor: Oyster bar and seafood spot, a St. Pete fixture since 1999, now in Grand Central

the-palladium-theater.text: Built in 1925 as the First Church of Christ, Scientist, and designed by Howard Lovewell Cheney after Brunelleschi's Ospedale degli Innocenti in Florence, the building became a concert hall in 1998 and has been run by St. Petersburg College since 2007. Its century-old Skinner pipe organ was donated to a Snell Isle church in 2025 to free up stage space ahead of the theater's centennial.
the-palladium-theater.descriptor: 1925 church turned concert hall on 5th Ave N; home of Hough Hall

the-pizza-joint-fl.text: A locally owned slice counter with chef Ariel Hernandez in the kitchen: the specialty slice rotates by the day (buffalo chicken lands on Wednesdays), and two slices with a drink is the standing cheap-lunch deal. Beyond pizza it runs a full red-sauce menu — mussels marinara with linguine and chicken parmigiana among them.
the-pizza-joint-fl.descriptor: Slice shop on 49th Street N in Pinellas Park with a daily specialty slice

the-tap-room.text: The in-house restaurant of the Hollander Hotel on 4th Ave N, serving breakfast through dinner seven days a week. It's known for filet mignon, grouper nuggets and a Cuban quesadilla, plus a bakery case of pastries and cakes poured alongside locally roasted Kahwa coffee; locals get 25% off on Thursdays.
the-tap-room.descriptor: Breakfast-to-dinner restaurant and bar inside the Hollander Hotel on 4th Ave N

the-tavern-at-bayboro.text: Open since 1982 beside the USF St. Pete campus, this locals' bar has had four owners and is known for its grouper sandwich, a perennial Best of the Bay nominee made with Tarpon Springs fish in a cornflake-almond crust. Its Wednesday open mic has run since 2010, with house guitars for anyone who forgot theirs.
the-tavern-at-bayboro.descriptor: Campus-side tavern by USF St. Pete known for its grouper sandwich, since 1982

the-toasted-monkey.text: A funky Old Florida beach bar with daily live music, a dog-friendly deck and a scratch kitchen. It spent eight years at the Howard Johnson hotel down the road before moving to bring the corner of Sunset Way and 75th Avenue back to life.
the-toasted-monkey.descriptor: Old Florida beach bar and scratch kitchen at Sunset & 75th Ave, St. Pete Beach

the-wharf.text: A family-owned Pass-a-Grille waterfront spot for more than 30 years, housed in a roughly 100-year-old building that was recently designated a local historic site. Boaters tie up at its docks for an oversized blackened grouper sandwich and grouper tacos with sweet Thai chile sauce.
the-wharf.descriptor: Waterfront seafood bar with boat docks on Pass-a-Grille Way, 30+ years

the-wooden-rooster.text: A downtown creperie on 2nd Ave NE whose signature savory crepe is named "The Burg" (caramelized onions, mushrooms, scrambled eggs and asiago); it grew popular enough that in 2018 it announced a second location in Seminole City Center.
the-wooden-rooster.descriptor: Breakfast-and-lunch creperie on 2nd Ave NE, downtown

three-birds-tavern.text: The 140-year-old farmhouse, one of the original home sites in southern Pinellas County, had already housed restaurants for years when Robin and Jack King bought what was then Limey's in June 2009. Robin named it after Bob Marley's 'Three Little Birds,' a song she tied to her late mother, and the couple's restoration of the house and its towering oaks won a city beautification award in 2015; they sold to John and Haley Ruetz in 2021.
three-birds-tavern.descriptor: American tavern in a 140-year-old farmhouse on 4th St N with oak-shaded patios

thuy-cafe.descriptor: Family-run Vietnamese bánh mì and boba shop in a strip mall on 34th St N

tobys-original-little-italy-pizza.text: Tobia "Toby" Spinelli, a native of Naples, Italy, opened this pizzeria in the Disston Plaza shopping center in 1972, and it has stayed with the same two families ever since — a strip-mall counter-service spot that locals swear by for New York-style pies, garlic knots and a Philly cheesesteak.
tobys-original-little-italy-pizza.descriptor: New York-style pizza and subs in Disston Plaza since 1972

tonys-pizza.text: Downtown's late-night slice stop: New York-style pies sold by the slice under the tagline "Simply the Best Pizza in DTSP," with the counter open until 3 a.m. on Fridays and Saturdays.
tonys-pizza.descriptor: New York-style pizza by the slice on Central Ave, open late

trailer-daddy.text: Trailer Daddy opened in March 2026 in the old Glamper space at 217 Central Ave, kitted out with vintage campers, lawn flamingos, year-round Christmas lights and a turf-floored outdoor bar. Its backstory is invented: a Pensacola used-car salesman named Waylon "Daddy" Whitley who hit a $50,000 gas-station scratch-off. Inside there's a Mullet Hall of Fame, stocked by a Best Mullet Contest on opening weekend.
trailer-daddy.descriptor: Retro trailer-park-themed bar on Central Ave, open since March 2026

treasure-bay-resort-and-marina.descriptor: Budget hotel and marina across the street from the beach in Treasure Island

trips-diner.text: Opened March 12, 2012 in the old Dave's diner space and named for the owners' triplets — Libby, Will and John. Owner Gordon Stevenson built the resin-topped tables himself, embedding vintage St. Pete postcards and tourism brochures, and the walls hang with Burgert Brothers photos; one regular spotted his own father in a picture over a corner booth.
trips-diner.descriptor: Breakfast-all-day neighborhood diner on MLK St N since 2012

tritons-pub.text: This is Eckerd College's campus pub, run by the school's food-service contractor Bon Appétit. A 2022 makeover added a long family-style wooden table down the middle, pushed closing time from 10 p.m. to 1 a.m., and put mushroom Phillys and cod tacos alongside the curly fries and chicken tenders students actually come for.
tritons-pub.descriptor: Eckerd College campus pub and late-night grill on 54th Ave S

trophy-fish.text: Opened June 1, 2018 on Central Ave as an outdoor-only patio fish house with a daily-changing menu built on the local catch and a 'Boat Drinks' cocktail list that won the Tampa Bay Times' Best Cocktail List in 2019. It's run by Seed & Feed Hospitality Group and has since added a second location on N Florida Ave in Tampa.
trophy-fish.descriptor: 'Bait shop chic' patio fish house with Boat Drinks on Central Ave since 2018

tropicana-field.text: Opened in 1990 as the Florida Suncoast Dome before any team had signed on, it has been the Rays' home since 1998 and is MLB's only fixed-roof dome; its slanted roof and catwalk rings have famously interfered with play. Hurricane Milton shredded the roof in October 2024, sending the Rays to Tampa for all of 2025 until a nearly $60M repair brought them back for the April 2026 home opener.
tropicana-field.descriptor: Domed MLB ballpark, home of the Rays since 1998

tryst.text: Opened in spring 2016 by Paris-born Renaud Cowez, with a room designer Rob Bowen fitted out in tiled walls, a backlit onyx bar top and black lace-patterned wallpaper — a look Bowen said was inspired by lingerie. The Mediterranean-leaning menu is built around shareable plates and a French-style fruits de mer platter, and the bar stays open until 3 a.m.
tryst.descriptor: Late-night Mediterranean gastro lounge on Beach Drive across from the MFA

twin-brooks-golf-course.text: The city's nine-hole par-3 course in South St. Pete is home to First Tee St. Petersburg's junior golf program, with a driving range and a three-hole practice area for the kids; it reopened after a refurbishment covered by the Tampa Bay Times.
twin-brooks-golf-course.descriptor: City-run 9-hole par-3 course and driving range at 3800 22nd Ave S

twisted-indian.descriptor: Indian fusion counter on Central Ave — naanwiches, bowls and tikka masala

undertow.text: A toes-in-the-sand tiki bar right on the beach at St. Pete Beach: thatched huts, volleyball nets, pool tables and frozen drinks in plastic cups. Its quirk is a "rubber duck river" that flows around the bar, and I Love the Burg has called it one of the most scenic beach bars in America.
undertow.descriptor: Open-air tiki beach bar on the sand at 3850 Gulf Blvd, St. Pete Beach

valentys-lounge.text: Tucked behind Pasadena Liquors, Valenty's is a time capsule: the interior copies a kiosk bar that founder John Valenty saw at the Pittsburgh airport, and his son Jim, a former elementary school teacher, has run it since 1990 with the original furniture, a piano, free popcorn, $2 beers and a house whiskey old fashioned.
valentys-lounge.descriptor: Family-run cocktail lounge behind a liquor store, known for cheap old fashioneds

victors-kitchen.text: A hole-in-the-wall breakfast counter at 5571 Park Blvd that opens at 7am and locks up at 2:30pm, closed Mondays. Regulars come for the pancakes, biscuits and gravy, French toast and country fried steak rather than anything fancy.
victors-kitchen.descriptor: Breakfast-and-lunch diner on Park Blvd, Pinellas Park; closed Mondays

vinoy-park.text: This 11.6-acre stretch of downtown waterfront takes its name from the neighboring Vinoy Park Hotel, built in 1925. It is the city's go-to outdoor event lawn, hosting the Tampa Bay Blues Festival, Ribfest, concerts, art festivals and triathlons.
vinoy-park.descriptor: Downtown waterfront park and festival lawn beside the Vinoy hotel

webbs-city-cellar.text: Green Bench Brewing's second tasting room, opened in 2019 next to the brewery on Baum Ave, is named for Webb's City, Doc Webb's self-styled "World's Most Unusual Drug Store" that sprawled across downtown St. Pete from 1926 to 1979 with 77 departments and in-store sideshows. The climate-controlled cellar holds up to 700 wine barrels of sour and wild ales, plus house mead and cider.
webbs-city-cellar.descriptor: Green Bench's barrel-aged sour, mead and cider tasting room on Baum Ave, since 2019

welcome-to-the-farm.text: Country singer Chase Rice's farmhouse-themed bar, opened November 2022 with Ohio's Forward Hospitality Group in the former MacDinton's space on the Jannus block. Modeled on Rice's family farm ('a lot more alcohol,' he said), it pours nearly 100 whiskeys and hosts live country music.
welcome-to-the-farm.descriptor: Country bar with live music on the Jannus block of 1st Ave N, since 2022

welton-brewing-co.text: Cousins Brandon and Sean Welton, both from Damariscotta, Maine, moved their brewery here from Land O' Lakes in March 2024 and pair their house beers with Damariscotta oysters, lobster rolls and clam chowder. One cousin got into brewing while running a beer-review website in the late 1990s, and their beers won Clearwater's Oktoberfest tournament.
welton-brewing-co.descriptor: Maine-style brewery and oyster bar on 66th St N in Pinellas Park

welton-brewing-company-and-oyster-bar.text: Started by cousins Brandon and Sean Welton (Brandon a 22-year Air Force veteran) after their garage homebrew won at Clearwater's Oktoberfest, the brewery launched in Land O' Lakes in 2020 and reopened in Pinellas Park in March 2024. The cousins' Damariscotta, Maine roots explain the menu: Damariscotta River oysters, lobster rolls, clam chowder and whoopie pies alongside the beer.
welton-brewing-company-and-oyster-bar.descriptor: Craft brewery and Maine-style oyster bar on 66th St N in Pinellas Park

writtenFor.name: Welton Brewing Company and Oyster Bar

wharf-seafood-restaurant.text: A Pass-a-Grille fixture for more than 30 years, housed in a roughly century-old building on the bayside where boaters tie up at the docks. The blackened grouper sandwich is the calling card the place is famous for, and there's live music on the front porch Wednesday through Saturday.
wharf-seafood-restaurant.descriptor: Bayside seafood spot on Pass-a-Grille Way known for its blackened grouper sandwich

wheres-jubes.text: Aussie brewpub opened June 2022 by Josh 'Jubes' Cameron, who moved from Dubbo, New South Wales to St. Pete in 2013 and also owns the Oyster Bar and Crafty Squirrel. Brewed with New Zealand brewmaster Brian Watson, its beers are named for Australian places, like Booti Booti Brut IPA, Bong Bong IPA and Wonglepong Light Lager.
wheres-jubes.descriptor: Australian brewpub on Central Ave with house beers named for Aussie towns

whiskey-on-park.descriptor: Pinellas Park bar on Park Blvd with pool tables, darts and karaoke

wild-child.text: Opened in summer 2020 in the former NuMex space by St. Pete natives Matt Kaye (also behind The Bends) and chef Rob Reinsmith, who came home after years in New York restaurants. The menu borrows from Tulum, the Caribbean and beyond — jerk octopus, snapper ceviche, a Korean fried chicken sandwich — under murals by local and Miami artists.
wild-child.descriptor: Tropical-leaning neighborhood bistro and cocktail bar on Central Ave in Grand Central

wildlife-acai.text: A Brazilian café where açaí bowls share the menu with tapioca crepes, pão de queijo cheese bread, cuscuz, and drinks made from tropical fruit pulps like cupuaçu and goiaba.
wildlife-acai.descriptor: Brazilian açaí and tapioca café on Park Blvd in Pinellas Park

williams-park.text: St. Petersburg's first park, laid out in 1888 as City Park and renamed for city co-founder John C. Williams; it fills a whole downtown block between 3rd and 4th Streets. A bandstand has stood here since 1894 - the current bandshell, designed by local architect William B. Harvard in 1954, won an AIA Award of Merit the next year - and in 1964 Richard Nixon used it to stump for Barry Goldwater.
williams-park.descriptor: Downtown's original city-block park with a 1954 bandshell, 4th St N at 2nd Ave N

woodson-african-american-museum.text: Housed in a former administrative office of Jordan Park, St. Petersburg's first Black public housing community, the museum opened in 2006 after a 1997 HUD Hope VI grant rebuilt the neighborhood. Local schoolchildren chose to name it for Carter G. Woodson, the historian who helped establish Black History Month. It rebranded as the Woodson African American Museum of Florida in 2021 and launched a capital campaign for a larger purpose-built home.
woodson-african-american-museum.descriptor: African American history and art museum in a former Jordan Park office building

world-vegan-cuisine.text: Everything here is plant-based: the kitchen makes freshly prepared vegan dishes drawn from cuisines all over the world. It sits in a suite on 34th Street North, away from St. Pete's downtown restaurant strips.
world-vegan-cuisine.descriptor: All-vegan kitchen on 34th St N serving globally inspired plates

wrigleys-pizza.text: A Chicago-transplant hangout on 4th Street North that used to trade as Paul's Chicago Pizza before rebranding as Wrigley's. It serves thin-crust (not deep-dish) Chicago pizza and Italian beef on Turano bread shipped from Chicago, with 22 TVs, every Cubs game on the MLB package and official Bears-bar status.
wrigleys-pizza.descriptor: Chicago thin-crust pizza and Italian beef sports bar on 4th St N

yummy-thai.descriptor: Thai restaurant with a weekday lunch buffet on Roosevelt Blvd

zaytoon-grill.descriptor: Greek-Mediterranean grill at 1618 Central Ave in the Edge District

zekos-mediterranian-grill.text: The St. Pete outpost of a small Tampa Bay chain (its two Tampa locations run until 4 a.m.), pitching a lighter 'Fresh-Med' take on shawarma, gyro and kebab plates with hummus made by hand daily from organic chickpeas.
zekos-mediterranian-grill.descriptor: Mediterranean shawarma, gyro and kebab grill on 54th Ave N

zom-hee-chinese-restaurant.text: Family-owned since 1985 in Seminole's Park Place Center on Park Blvd, Zom Hee cooks Szechuan, Hunan and Cantonese dishes in a 250-seat dining room with a cocktail lounge pouring Mai Tais, Blue Hawaiis and a house drink called the Confucius Itch.
zom-hee-chinese-restaurant.descriptor: Family-run Szechuan/Hunan/Cantonese restaurant on Park Blvd in Seminole since 1985

baba.text: George and Debbie Sayegh, the couple behind Bodega, opened Baba in June 2019 as a Greek-Lebanese restaurant named for their fathers: baba means dad in both languages. In 2023 they added Barbouni, a nine-seat sister spot. Both closed after service on July 3, 2026, with longtime team members reopening the space as Barra Barra and Kaixo.
baba.descriptor: Greek-Lebanese restaurant at 2701 Central in the Grand Central District (2019-2026)

the-neon-lunchbox.text: An '80s/'90s-themed restaurant, bar and music venue that opened in March 2024 in the old Hideaway Cafe space, with murals of nostalgic pop-culture icons, a glow-in-the-dark VIP room, a horror-movie bathroom, and a New Orleans-leaning menu from the couple behind the Half Baked Potato. Patrons could donate vintage items for decor in exchange for a discount. It closed on August 29, 2026, with the owners citing rising costs and health issues.
the-neon-lunchbox.descriptor: Retro '80s/'90s restaurant, bar and stage at 1756 Central Ave (closed Aug 2026)

thirsty-first.text: CLOSED July 26, 2026. Thirsty First opened on 1st Ave N in 2016 as a craft-cocktail lounge with lockers where regulars kept their own bottles, then grew into a sports bar and in May 2025 moved into the former Acropolis Greek Taverna building at 515 Central: nearly 9,000 square feet, two stories and 69 TVs. Owner Greg Mikurak shut it down in 2026 after a lease dispute and rising costs.
thirsty-first.descriptor: Two-story sports bar with 69 TVs at 515 Central Ave (closed 2026)
